value.name: AEP Ohio
value.notes: Ohio is a retail-choice state — customers may select a Competitive Retail Electric Service (CRES) provider for generation while AEP Ohio remains the distribution utility. No specific CCA or default CRES provider was independently confirmed for Columbus residential solar customers this session; AEP Ohio is recorded as the default (non-shopping) generation/distribution utility.

permit_authority.value: City of Columbus Building and Zoning Services (BZS)
permit_authority.notes: Ohio's building code (Ohio Building Code / Ohio Residential Code) is adopted at the state level by the Ohio Board of Building Standards, but enforcement is local — Columbus's own Building and Zoning Services department is the AHJ within city limits.

interconnection_url.notes: Confirmed directly from AEP Ohio's own filed PUCO tariff (P.U.C.O. No. 20, Schedule NEMS, effective 2012-01-01): net metering is available to solar/wind/biomass/landfill-gas/hydropower/microturbine/fuel-cell generators located on the customer's premises. Sizing cap: the generating system must not produce more than 120% of the customer's electricity needs over a rolling 12-month period, or the account loses NEMS eligibility. AEP Ohio does not buy the electricity — a monetary credit is calculated only from the generation energy component of the standard service rate (not the full retail rate, and excluding distribution/transmission charges) and applied to the current or future bill; unused credits are lost if the customer stops service. A separate Schedule NEMS-H applies to hospital customers, crediting at the hourly AEP East Load Zone Real-Time Locational Marginal Price. Net metering requires a bidirectional meter (installed at customer expense if the existing meter can't measure two-way flow) and a completed Net Energy Metering Service Application plus a separate Interconnection Agreement.
